parsed.explanation: The combined regime's sharpest edge is the entry gate: national adjudication treats document/sex discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' about an applicant's sex as grounds to refuse and to consider a lifetime fraud finding, and allied governments issued trans-travel advisories after foreign nationals were detained over visa issues. Within the state, all schools and colleges must segregate facilities by birth certificate (no enforcement mechanism, no documented case), a care/sports ban is in litigation, and school staff must out LGBTQ students. National rules bar identity-congruent use of government-funded facilities, and the record documents severe abuse in immigration custody. Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity or presentation, no documented police campaign or street-violence pattern, working courts (injunctions, 2018 and 2020 rulings), national hate-crime and employment coverage, and marriage recognition.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable: discrepancy in documents/records or 'reasonable doubt' as to sex leads to refusal and demands for further evidence; suspected misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime ineligibility under the fraud ground. X markers no longer processed for new issues; athletes barred; neighbouring citizens documented detained over visa issues; allied advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; a fraud finding is never automatic, requires four elements, and limited waivers exist; policy under active litigation; legal-aid FAQ published for document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor carries a home-issued passport; exposure crystallises in national adjudication at the port, where officer discretion plus database mismatch decides.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: transgender men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Corrections policy since 2026 imposes hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution on trans inmates; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders enjoined; consular access for detained trans visitors not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can convert a traveller into a detainee, and custody then places by birth sex under the documented-abuse regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Statewide law requires every K-12 school and public and private college to designate bathrooms, locker rooms and overnight accommodation by birth certificate.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy facilities exempt; the state statute carries no enforcement mechanism and no arrest, citation or case is documented under it; chaperoning exemptions exist.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The national rule reaches federal sites a tourist uses; the state rule bites on enrolled students, so a visiting family with a minor at school is the exposed unit, not the lone adult tourist.

care_services.exposure: State bill bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s and bars trans girls and women from school and college sports; national order frames minor care as mutilation; proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18; 27 states ban care.
care_services.protection: The state ban was re-enjoined 18 March 2025; earlier adult-care rules requiring perpetual psychiatric oversight were dropped in 2024; a 2018 national appeals ruling covers the state.
care_services.interaction: Provider liability chills clinics even while enjoined, so a travelling family seeking care meets refusal rather than prosecution; the operative status of the state ban is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralisation' of groups described as radically pro-transgender; a justice-department reward memorandum uses 'radical gender ideology'; an order directs investigating schools and prosecuting teachers who affirm a trans minor's transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memorandum does not make gender ideology a reward criterion; the strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing targets advocacy and school staff rather than foreign visitors directly, but raises the political temperature and the risk of hostile official encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: State law obliges school staff to disclose a student's LGBTQ status to parents and removes undefined 'gender ideology' from K-3 curricula; the facility law assigns students to birth-certificate facilities; the under-18 care ban (enjoined) would block a visiting minor's treatment.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental opt-out for remaining curricular material; care ban currently enjoined; chaperoning and disability/emergency exemptions in the facility statute.
minors_guardians.interaction: Mandated outing and facility assignment operate through enrolment, so a tourist family is largely outside them unless the minor attends school; a care-seeking family faces provider refusal.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Polling shows 66% support for birth-sex document laws and 69% for birth-sex sports alignment — disapproval expressed through law, not documented confrontation. No trans-specific violence pattern in this state is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 33 cities and counties bar gender-identity discrimination; no sodomy law; no documented police campaign against trans people here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Ordinary tourist settings (hotels, transit, venues) are covered by no state public-accommodation statute, so a refusal would leave municipal ordinance or national law as the only route.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The July 2026 tiering methodology is unstated; the motor-vehicle marker rule's final text, effective date and any challenge are unsourced; which counties refuse birth-certificate corrections is unsourced; the care and sports bans' operative status is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts demonstrably act: 2020 invalidation of the birth-certificate bar, March 2025 re-enjoinment, injunctions against national orders; national hate-crime and employment coverage remain in force.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work but slowly and unevenly, and a short-stay visitor cannot realistically litigate a refusal before departing.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far safer than Oskara: no morality-unit street sweeps, no coerced confessions, no capital exposure, no documented police predation on gender-nonconforming people, and courts here grant relief. Oskara's organised targeting with the state's own hand dominates this dossier's conditional institutional exposures.

Broadly comparable, slightly worse in severity. Vellandra refuses visibly trans visitors routinely but stops at exclusion. Here the entry gate is not trans-targeted as such yet escalates: refusal, a possible lifetime fraud finding, and documented severe abuse in immigration custody downstream.

Worse than Kestrel Isles. That dossier's worst outcome is humiliating secondary screening, denied admission and cost, with no custody harm documented. Here secondary scrutiny feeds a fraud ground with permanent effect and a custody regime whose abuse is documented.

Well below Meridia, where markers may match presentation, officers are trained, detention is brief and a tribunal orders release with compensation. Here no trans-specific criminalisation exists, but the border rule, facility segregation and custody record are operative and unremedied for a short-stay visitor.

Incomparably safer. Vellmar has enforced equality law, audited border conduct and remedies that change outcomes. This jurisdiction has no statewide public-accommodation protection, an active document-restriction programme, and oversight that has not altered the practices it records.

parsed.synthesis: For an adult travelling alone the daily exposure is moderate: no statute criminalises trans identity or presentation, no enforcement case exists under the school facility law, and ordinary commerce is largely untouched by it. The real exposure is at the threshold and in custody — a passport whose appearance and marker invite 'reasonable doubt' can produce refusal, a permanent ineligibility finding, or detention in a system whose abuse of trans detainees is documented. A family travelling with a minor faces the additional layer of facility assignment by birth certificate and mandated school disclosure, though only through enrolment. Working courts, national hate-crime coverage and marriage recognition offset the picture without reaching the border desk.
